# Verify user token

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:identity-verification` · **Epic:** [#20](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/20) · **Tickets:** 12 (9S 3M)

The worker reads a user token from Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT, or from X-Warden-Identity on HTTP that Warden terminates (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2). It captures the header BEFORE the existing proxy-only header strip runs, verifies the token against the issuer's JWKS, and then lets the strip (already on main) remove both headers before forwarding, in every mode. It records sub, verified email, groups and identity status on every event, receipt, decision log and fleet event. Each agent's identity mode is off (the default) or attribute. Attribute mode records identity and never blocks. Only status valid produces a policy subject, so later group and user rules can never match an unverified caller. Limit, stated plainly: in transparent mode (#376) there is no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization, so only X-Warden-Identity on terminated traffic can attribute there.

## How we build it

- New package `internal/identity` (no such package exists yet; go.mod gains `github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3` pinned to a release at least two weeks old; architecture.yaml gets a class for the package and an S3 module-manifest entry). It defines `Claims{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, SID, Issuer, AZP, Nonce, IssuedAt, Expiry}`, the policy subject `Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID}` with `SubjectFrom(claims, status) *Subject` (nil unless status is valid; p1-group-policy, p1-block-list and later per-user features use this one type), `Status` (off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict), a bounded `Reason` (bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, malformed, too_large, ttl_too_long, jwks_unavailable) and the interface `Verifier.Verify(ctx, raw string, opts ...VerifyOption) (Claims, Status, Reason)`. There is no `StripHeaders` function: stripping already exists in internal/proxy/hopheaders.go. A fake verifier lives in test/fakes and is registered as the fake of the new `identity.Verifier` port in test/harness/registry.go.
- OIDC verifier. `NewOIDCVerifier(Config{Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, ClockSkew, MaxTokenTTL, GroupsClaim, InternalIssuerURL, CAFile})` does no network I/O at construction. Discovery (when JWKSURL is empty) and JWKS fetches happen lazily. They use the one shared client of W-P1-VRFY-12 (identity.NewHTTPClient: Proxy=nil, a plain net.Dialer and not the proxy SafeDialer so an issuer on a private network such as Dex on cp-net is reachable, a 5s timeout, a capped response body), handed to go-oidc and golang.org/x/oauth2 through identity.WithHTTPClient. Split-horizon: the issuer string is the public one (dev: `http://localhost:5556/dex`, what browsers and host CLIs see); when `InternalIssuerURL` is set (containers, e.g. `http://dex:5556`), requests whose origin equals the issuer's origin go to the internal origin, changing only scheme, host and port of the TCP destination, so the issuer, `iss`, path, headers and body never change and go-oidc's issuer checks pass. A plain-http issuer is accepted only when InternalIssuerURL is set (the dev profile); otherwise https is required. There is no insecure flag. A Warden wrapper around the go-oidc key set allows at most one unknown-kid refetch per 30s per issuer (singleflight plus an interval floor) and keeps the last good keyset while fetches fail. Warden enforces this itself and does not rely on go-oidc to limit refetches. Allowed algorithms are exactly RS256 and ES256. The verifier checks iss exactly, checks that aud contains Audience, and checks azp against AllowedAZP when that list is set. exp and nbf are checked in Warden with ClockSkew (default 60s, max 5m), and exp-iat must not exceed MaxTokenTTL (default 1h). Tokens over 16 KiB are rejected before parsing. Groups are read from GroupsClaim (default `groups`), sorted, de-duplicated and capped at 64 entries of 256 bytes, with GroupsTruncated set. Email is lowercased and kept only when email_verified is not false. A bounded LRU (10k entries) keyed by sha256(token) caches results until min(exp, now+5m), and exp is re-checked on every hit. `WithNonce` lets the CP console login (W-P1-SSO-03) reuse the verifier with its own audience.
- Config (W-P1-VRFY-08). `SettingsWire.Identity *IdentitySettings{DefaultMode, Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, GroupsClaim, ClockSkewSeconds, MaxTokenTTLSeconds, InternalIssuerURL}` (json `identity`, omitempty; absent means off). A matching local `identity:` YAML block serves standalone workers. Per-agent override is a new `Identity string` field added to both the existing `AgentSettings` and `config.AgentPolicy` (and rawAgent), so the existing `AgentSettings(a)` conversion in SettingsWireFromPolicy keeps compiling. A worker resolves its mode for the agent ID that `worker.defaultAgentID` already computes (Agents[0].ID, or `agent:<port>` via agentid.PortBindingIdentifier). Validation on the CP and locally accepts off|attribute and rejects `require` with a 'Phase 2' error; a worker's parseRemotePolicy does not reject a served wire for an unsupported mode, which W-P1-VRFY-07 handles by keeping the previous identity config. An http issuer is rejected unless `internalIssuerURL` is set (the W-P1-VRFY-12 rule); `internalIssuerURL` is optional, must be an absolute http(s) URL with no path beyond `/`, and needs a non-empty issuer. The block holds no secrets. The CP settings writer (WriteSettings) must carry the block so a dashboard settings edit never drops it.
- Hot reload. The verifier lives in a new atomic holder `identityP` on Proxy (same pattern as secretsP and judgeP). The SettingsApplier rebuilds the verifier only when the issuer, internalIssuerURL, audience, JWKS URL, azp, skew or TTL settings change, so the key cache survives unrelated applies. If a rebuild fails, or a newer CP sends an unknown mode, the worker keeps the previous identity config and logs one warning. In-flight connections keep their snapshot.
- Extraction (W-P1-VRFY-02). `handleConn` (internal/proxy/serve.go) captures Proxy-Authorization in its existing bounded CONNECT header loop: Basic with username `session` (the password is the token) or Bearer. Any other form, or more than one Proxy-Authorization line, gives status invalid with reason malformed. Verification runs before `Policy.EvaluateRequest`, so CONNECT deny events are attributed too. The result is a per-connection `connIdentity{Claims, Status, Reason, Expiry}` passed to handleTLS, tunnel, handleHTTP and handleGRPC. The worker consumes the CONNECT request, so this header is never forwarded. X-Warden-Identity: Bearer is honored only on HTTP that Warden terminates. ORDER MATTERS: `stripHopHeaders` (internal/proxy/hopheaders.go) runs right after `readRequest` in runRequestStages and deletes Proxy-Authorization, Proxy-Connection and X-Warden-Identity, so the raw X-Warden-Identity value must be captured onto requestScope immediately BEFORE that call, and the new `identityStage` (verification) runs right after the strip and before constraintGate and judgeGate; an identityStage that read the header after the strip would always see it empty. HTTP/2 and gRPC streams run the same runRequestStages pipeline (`serveGRPCStream`, #388), so this one capture covers them too; `copyGRPCHeaders` only strips on the upstream hop, after the capture. Raw tunnels (no CA, non-TLS traffic, unknown protocols inside TLS) are opaque: they carry only the CONNECT identity, and the worker logs one startup warning when attribute mode is on and no CA is configured. Transparent mode (#376) has no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization: its listeners pass a zero connIdentity (status none), only X-Warden-Identity on terminated traffic attributes there, and the startup warning also covers a transparent-only worker.
- Stripping is unconditional and already on main (#396): `proxyOnlyHeaders` in internal/proxy/hopheaders.go is applied by `stripHopHeaders` on every terminated HTTP/1.1 request and by `copyGRPCHeaders` on every h2 stream, in every mode, including when there are no identity settings, so a user token never reaches an upstream from traffic Warden terminates. This feature adds no stripping code; it only has to read the identity header before that strip runs, and keeps a regression test that the upstream never sees either header.
- Status rules in attribute mode never block a request. A valid CONNECT identity applies to the connection until its exp (plus skew) passes; later requests on that connection get status expired. A per-request header applies when CONNECT carried no token. Two valid identities with different sub give status conflict and no subject, and the request proceeds; a 403 identity_conflict is reserved for require mode in P2. A token sent while mode is off gives status off with no verification. Keys that cannot be fetched give unverified, which is kept distinct from invalid. Only status valid yields a non-nil `identity.Subject` for p1-group-policy, p1-block-list and later per-user features. Every other status is treated as anonymous, so group- and user-scoped rules never match and default-deny holds. sub is the authoritative key for user rules, and email matching requires a verified email.
- Recording. `analytics.Event` gains `UserSub, UserEmail, UserGroups, UserGroupsTruncated, UserSID, IdentityStatus, IdentityReason` with explicit snake_case json tags and omitempty (Event has no tags today except UID), stored by W-P1-VRFY-03. Unattributed events, receipts and sync payloads therefore stay byte-identical, and old receipts keep verifying because Receipt keeps the signed EventJSON bytes. Every proxy event is stored through one new `p.recordEvent(ci connIdentity, e analytics.Event)`, which stamps the identity fields (W-P1-VRFY-09). It replaces the direct StoreEvent calls in secretscope.go, serve.go, ws.go, tls.go (two sites), http.go (two sites) and the deny chokepoint `emitDenyEventDetail` in deny.go; grpc.go has no direct StoreEvent. Pre-CONNECT parse failures pass the zero connIdentity. decisionLog adds user_sub, identity_status, identity_reason and groups_count. Email and the group list appear in operational logs only at debug level. The raw token is never logged, stored, signed, put in an error body or passed to the judge or MCP gateway.
- Storage. The local SQLiteStore (W-P1-VRFY-03) gets additive addColumnIfAbsent migrations for user_sub, user_email, user_groups (a JSON array, because LDAP DN group names contain commas), user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status and identity_reason, plus an index on (user_sub, ts). The columns are added to insertColumns, the GetEvents scan and the GetOldestEventIDs SELECT and scan, which is the SyncWorker source. FleetSQLiteStore.migrate is a bare CREATE TABLE today, so the fleet side (W-P1-VRFY-06) gets a new idempotent addColumnIfAbsent helper, the same columns and indexes, and extended StoreAggregatedEvent INSERT and GetEvents scans. Rollout order is CP first, then workers. A version mismatch drops or empties the fields and never errors.
- Observability. A nil-safe `(*Metrics).RecordIdentityVerify(result, reason)` registers the OTel counter `warden.identity.verify.total{result,reason}` with bounded labels; P2 extends this instrument and does not add a new one. `RecordJWKSFetch(result)` registers `warden.identity.jwks.fetch.total{result}`. Identity time is recorded in the existing `warden.request.added_latency` histogram with stage=identity. Budget: p99 under 100µs for a cached token, and under 1ms uncached excluding key fetches.
- Dashboard. `analytics.EventFilter.User` matches user_sub exactly or lower(user_email), using parameterized SQL only (W-P1-VRFY-04). It is exposed as `?user=` on /dashboard/api/traffic and /dashboard/api/analytics on worker and CP, and the analytics cache key includes the normalized user. The analytics top-users table and the UI user column and filter box (W-P1-VRFY-10) render claim values with textContent only. The Query Builder schema already comes from PRAGMA table_info, so the user columns appear in it with no code change.
- Deployment and docs. Workers need egress to the issuer for discovery and JWKS, so deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml and the compose templates allow worker to issuer traffic. docs/control-plane.md documents the identity block, the per-agent field, the transport rules (X-Warden-Identity only with TLS termination; Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT works everywhere and is recommended) and the rollout order. They also state that a P1 identity is a bearer assertion signed by the IdP and not yet bound to the agent; P2 adds binding and bundle-distributed JWKS.
- Size limits, fixed for P1 and used everywhere (the identity contract, the exec forwarder, the P2 forwarder and token service): a token is at most 16 KiB (larger is invalid with reason too_large before parsing). The CONNECT limits already exist on main and need no code here: the request line is capped at 8 KiB (414), the whole header block at 64 KiB with a 10 s deadline; overflow gets 431 and a deny event with reason malformed_connect and detail headers_too_large. 64 KiB leaves room for a 16 KiB token base64-encoded in Basic credentials.
- Test layers: unit tests per package; L1 scenarios on test/harness (in-process worker and CP, the in-process OIDC issuer fake from W-P1-VRFY-11, scenarios in W-P1-VRFY-05); the real-Dex proof is the L2 curl-agent smoke in p1-identity-contract (W-P1-IDC-03) on the shared stack from p1-dex (W-P1-DEX-04). test/integration holds only TestSingleBinary, and CI already runs `scripts/check.sh --integration`.
- Provider neutrality and one conformance suite: no non-test Go file under internal/ or cmd/ mentions Dex (guard test in W-P1-VRFY-01), and `identitytest.RunVerifierSuite` is run by both the real OIDC verifier and `fakes.Verifier`, so the fake cannot drift from the real behaviour.

## Done when

On a real deployment (CP plus at least one worker with TLS termination, Dex from p1-dex) with an agent in attribute mode, a request with a valid Dex token produces a local event, a signed receipt, a decision log line and a CP fleet event. Each carries the user's sub, verified email and groups with identity_status=valid. This holds for Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT and for X-Warden-Identity, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (transparent mode attributes only through X-Warden-Identity). The upstream never sees X-Warden-Identity or Proxy-Authorization on any terminated path, in any mode (regression test; the strip itself is on main). Invalid, expired, conflicting and missing tokens, and tokens sent while Dex is unreachable, are recorded as invalid, expired, conflict, none and unverified respectively, have no policy subject, and are allowed. The worker starts and serves traffic with Dex down. warden.identity.verify.total reports each outcome. Existing warden.db and fleet DB files upgrade in place with no data loss, and existing receipts still verify. A token minted for a host client at `http://localhost:5556/dex` verifies on a worker whose container reaches Dex through `identity.internalIssuerURL` (split-horizon, no hosts entry, no test-only dialer). Proven by: L1 scenarios `go test ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/identity_'` (W-P1-VRFY-05) and the L2 smoke `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestIdentitySmoke` (W-P1-IDC-03).

### 1/12 · W-P1-VRFY-01

**Add internal/identity OIDC verifier with lazy JWKS, cache and config**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#21](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/21)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20) lets a worker attribute traffic to a verified user. This is the foundation ticket (#21): the new package internal/identity that turns a raw OIDC token into Claims, a Status and a bounded Reason, and a fake for the tests that need it. Construction is lazy and never blocks, so the verifier can be built when Dex is down. Warden enforces the refetch floor, the exp/nbf skew and the size limits itself, so attribution never depends on library defaults. Nothing is wired into the proxy, so merging changes no behaviour. It depends on W-P1-VRFY-12 (the shared OIDC HTTP client with the internal-origin rewrite, the http-issuer rule and the package scaffold with its go-oidc architecture entries); this ticket builds no HTTP client of its own. Split from the original M ticket #21: the identity settings block (SettingsWire, local YAML, per-agent field, validation) moved to W-P1-VRFY-08, and `StripHeaders` was dropped because header stripping already exists on main (internal/proxy/hopheaders.go, #396). Siblings: VRFY-08 (config), VRFY-02 (proxy wiring), VRFY-03 and VRFY-09 (recording), VRFY-11 (OIDC issuer fake for tests). The CP console login (W-P1-SSO-03) later reuses this verifier through `WithNonce`.

What to build: create internal/identity with Claims, Status/Reason, the Verifier interface and an OIDC verifier on go-oidc v3 (lazy JWKS discovery, rate-limited key refetch, bounded result cache, size and time checks enforced by Warden itself), plus fakes.Verifier for tests and ONE conformance suite (identitytest.RunVerifierSuite) that both the real verifier and the fake pass. Architecture gate: the `internal/identity` class, zone and the go-oidc S3 entry come from W-P1-VRFY-12; this ticket adds only the new package `internal/identity/identitytest` (class testutil, zone shared). Run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` after editing architecture.yaml.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- In internal/identity (the package is created by W-P1-VRFY-12): Claims{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, SID (optional), Issuer, AZP, Nonce, IssuedAt, Expiry}, Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, AgentID} and SubjectFrom(claims, status) *Subject, which copies GroupsTruncated from Claims and returns nil for every status except valid, Status off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict, a bounded Reason set (bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, malformed, too_large, ttl_too_long, jwks_unavailable) and Verify(ctx, raw, opts...) (Claims, Status, Reason). There is NO StripHeaders function: stripping is on main in internal/proxy/hopheaders.go.
- NewOIDCVerifier(Config{Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, ClockSkew, MaxTokenTTL, GroupsClaim, InternalIssuerURL, CAFile}) on github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3 (dependency and architecture entry added by W-P1-VRFY-12). There is no insecure-issuer option: NewOIDCVerifier calls identity.CheckIssuer first, so a plain-http issuer is refused unless InternalIssuerURL is set (the dev profile). It allows only RS256 and ES256, checks iss exactly, checks that aud contains Audience, and checks azp against AllowedAZP when that list is set.
- Warden checks exp and nbf with ClockSkew (default 60s, max 5m) and rejects exp-iat above MaxTokenTTL (default 1h). It rejects tokens over 16 KiB with reason too_large before parsing. Confirm against the pinned go-oidc version which built-in time checks must be disabled.
- No network I/O at construction. Discovery and JWKS fetches are lazy and go through the shared client built by identity.NewHTTPClient (W-P1-VRFY-12: Proxy=nil, plain net.Dialer, 5s timeout, capped body, optional CA file, internal-origin rewrite) and handed to go-oidc with identity.WithHTTPClient, so discovery and JWKS fetches reach an internal issuer URL while the issuer string stays public. This ticket constructs no second client. An unknown kid triggers at most one refetch per 30s (singleflight plus an interval floor), and the last good keyset is kept. A failure to obtain keys returns status unverified with reason jwks_unavailable.
- Groups come from GroupsClaim (default groups) and are sorted, de-duplicated and capped at 64 entries of 256 bytes, with Claims.GroupsTruncated set to true when the token held more than 64 groups or any group over 256 bytes was dropped or cut (false otherwise, including when the claim is absent). SubjectFrom copies it to Subject.GroupsTruncated, so the group-policy tickets (group C) can fail closed on a truncated list instead of treating the missing groups as "not a member". Email is lowercased and kept only when email_verified is not false; EmailVerified is true only when the claim is literally true. A bounded LRU (10k entries) keyed by sha256(token) caches results until min(exp, now+5m), and exp is re-checked on every hit.
- Architecture gate: `internal/identity` and go-oidc are already registered by W-P1-VRFY-12. Add the new package `internal/identity/identitytest` to the `testutil` class paths and to the `shared` zone in architecture.yaml, like internal/clock/clocktest; run `go run ./cmd/archgen` so .golangci.arch.yml is regenerated, then `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture`. Each package needs a _test.go (rule C3).
- Raw tokens never appear in errors, logs or test output; only bounded reasons do. WithNonce(n) lets W-P1-SSO-03 reuse the verifier with its own audience.
- Add fakes.Verifier (map from token to Claims/Status/Reason, safe for concurrent use, counts calls) to test/fakes, and register it in test/harness/registry.go as the fake of the new `identity.Verifier` port with the shared conformance suite of the next requirement, so TestPortCoverage passes (a port interface with no registered fake fails CI).
- For status expired and for invalid with reason bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, unknown_kid or ttl_too_long, Verify still returns the sub and email parsed from a well-formed payload, so W-P1-BLOCK-02 can deny on a match (a match can only deny). These claims never yield a Subject and are never cached as valid. malformed and too_large return empty Claims.
- One conformance suite for the verifier seam: new package internal/identity/identitytest (imports only internal/identity and the standard library; it must NOT import test/fakes or test/harness, so there is no cycle) with `RunVerifierSuite(t *testing.T, factory Factory)`, `type Factory func(t *testing.T) Fixture` and `Fixture{Verifier identity.Verifier; Prepare func(Case) string}`. `Prepare` arranges the world for a Case and returns the raw token to present: the real-verifier fixture signs with per-test RS256/ES256 keys against an httptest JWKS (and stops that server for the issuer-down case), the fake fixture registers a token with the outcome the Case demands. Cases, each asserting Status, Reason, the sub and email carried per requirement 8, that SubjectFrom returns nil unless valid and that no raw token appears in any error: valid, expired, wrong-aud, wrong-azp, unknown-kid, truncated groups (100 groups: 64 kept, GroupsTruncated true) and issuer-down with a cold cache (unverified, jwks_unavailable). BOTH implementations run the same suite: `internal/identity/oidc_suite_test.go` (package identity_test) for NewOIDCVerifier, and `test/fakes/verifier_test.go` for fakes.Verifier; the registry.go conformance entry calls it too.
- Provider-neutral code: guard test `TestNoProviderSpecificCode` in internal/identity (package identity_test) walks every non-test .go file under `internal/` (and `cmd/`) and fails, naming file and line, when one matches the case-insensitive whole word `dex` (regexp `(?i)\bdex\b`, so `index` is fine) in an identifier, string or comment. Dex-specific names and URLs live only in compose files, configs, scripts and docs; no code path special-cases an IdP.
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the `internal/identity/identitytest` entry to architecture.yaml (testutil class, shared zone); create the new internal/identity/identity.go with Claims, Subject, SubjectFrom, Status, Reason, Verifier and VerifyOption/WithNonce.
2. Add the new internal/identity/keyset.go: a rateLimitedKeySet wrapping the go-oidc remote key set (singleflight, 30s floor, last-good keys; the HTTP client comes from W-P1-VRFY-12), plus lazy discovery when JWKSURL is empty.
3. Add the new internal/identity/oidc.go: NewOIDCVerifier with algorithm allowlist, iss/aud/azp checks, Warden-side exp/nbf/TTL checks, size cap, groups and email normalisation, and an error-to-Reason mapping (errors.As on the go-oidc expiry error).
4. Add the new internal/identity/cache.go: a bounded LRU keyed by sha256(token) with expiry at min(exp, now+5m).
5. Create internal/identity/identitytest (suite and Case table), add fakes.Verifier to test/fakes/fakes.go and its entry in test/harness/registry.go running the suite, and add `internal/identity/identitytest` to architecture.yaml.
6. Tests: the new internal/identity/oidc_test.go (httptest JWKS, RS256 and ES256 signers), keyset_test.go (rotation, refetch floor under -race, issuer down) and cache_test.go. The identity settings tests belong to W-P1-VRFY-08, not here.
7. Add oidc_suite_test.go and test/fakes/verifier_test.go running RunVerifierSuite, and the provider-neutrality guard test (it must pass on the tree as it is).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A valid token returns status valid with its Claims. Wrong iss, wrong aud, wrong azp, expired beyond 60s skew, nbf in the future, alg none, HS256 signed with the public key, exp-iat over 1h and a 17 KiB token each return the expected Status and Reason: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestOIDCVerifier`.
- [ ] After a JWKS rotation, a token with the new kid verifies after exactly one fetch, and 100 concurrent unknown-kid verifications within 30s cause at most one more fetch: `go test -race ./internal/identity -run TestJWKSRotation`.
- [ ] With the issuer unreachable, NewOIDCVerifier returns immediately, and Verify returns status unverified with reason jwks_unavailable within the context deadline: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestIssuerDown`.
- [ ] A group `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` survives intact, 100 groups are capped at 64 with Claims.GroupsTruncated=true and SubjectFrom copies it to Subject.GroupsTruncated=true (a token with 3 groups and a 300-byte group name also sets it; a token with 3 normal groups leaves both false), and email_verified=false leaves Email empty: `go test ./internal/identity -run 'TestGroups|TestEmail'`.
- [ ] An expired token and a token signed by an unknown key return their sub in Claims with status expired and invalid respectively, and SubjectFrom returns nil for both; a valid token with email_verified absent keeps Email but has EmailVerified=false: `go test ./internal/identity -run 'TestUnverifiedClaims|TestSubjectFrom'`.
- [ ] No raw token appears in any error string or captured log line: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestNoTokenInErrors`.
- [ ] `grep -rn StripHeaders internal/identity` prints nothing.
- [ ] `go test ./test/harness -run TestPortCoverage` passes with `identity.Verifier` registered, and `go test ./test/fakes` passes.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` passes with the identitytest package registered, and `scripts/check.sh` passes, including govulncheck.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestVerifierSuite` and `go test ./test/fakes -run TestVerifierSuite` both pass: the same identitytest.RunVerifierSuite covers valid, expired, wrong-aud, wrong-azp, unknown-kid, truncated groups and issuer-down for the real verifier and for fakes.Verifier (red first: a fake that returns valid for an expired Case fails the suite), and `go list -deps ./internal/identity/identitytest | grep -E 'test/(fakes|harness)'` prints nothing.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestNoProviderSpecificCode` passes and fails (red first) when a scratch file under internal/ names `Dex` in an identifier, string or comment; `grep -rniw dex internal cmd --include='*.go' --exclude='*_test.go'` prints nothing.
- [ ] A plain-http issuer is refused unless InternalIssuerURL is set, and an internal issuer URL is used for discovery and JWKS while the issuer string is unchanged: `go test ./internal/identity -run 'TestOIDCVerifierHTTPIssuerRule|TestOIDCVerifierInternalOrigin'` (the client itself is proven by W-P1-VRFY-12; this test proves the verifier uses it and builds no second client).

### 2/12 · W-P1-VRFY-02

**Extract and verify identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 before the proxy-only strip**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#22](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/22)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). This ticket (#22) wires the verifier into the proxy: it captures Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT and X-Warden-Identity on terminated HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, verifies both through a new identityP atomic holder, and carries the result on a per-connection connIdentity. It depends on W-P1-VRFY-01 (verifier and Status types). Stripping both headers before forwarding ALREADY exists on main (`stripHopHeaders` and `copyGRPCHeaders`, internal/proxy/hopheaders.go, #396), and so do the CONNECT header bounds (8 KiB line, 64 KiB block, 10 s deadline, 431 `malformed_connect` / `headers_too_large`). Both pieces of work were dropped from this ticket; what remains is to READ the header before the strip deletes it. Siblings: VRFY-03 and VRFY-09 (record the result on events and logs), VRFY-07 (builds the verifier on a real worker), VRFY-08 (config), VRFY-05 (L1 scenarios). Out of scope: event fields and storage (VRFY-03/09), config (VRFY-08), worker assembly and hot reload from settings (VRFY-07).

What to build: the identityP holder, the CONNECT extraction in handleConn, the pre-strip capture plus identityStage on HTTP/1.1, the status rules, the metric and the startup warning. With no identity configured nothing changes except the new capture, which reads a header the strip deletes anyway.

**Requirements**

- A new `identityP atomic.Pointer[identityHolder]` on Proxy with `identity()` and `SetIdentity(v identity.Verifier, mode)`, mirroring secretsP/judgeP, plus an optional `Identity` field on proxy.Config. A nil holder means mode off. The per-agent mode is passed in by the caller of SetIdentity (VRFY-07); this ticket only stores and reads it.
- CONNECT (internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn): capture `Proxy-Authorization` in the existing bounded header loop (Basic with username `session`, the password is the token; or Bearer). Any other form, or more than one Proxy-Authorization line, gives status invalid with reason malformed. Verify before `Policy.EvaluateRequest` with a 2 s context, so CONNECT deny events are attributable. The result is a `connIdentity{Claims, Status, Reason, Expiry}` passed to handleTLS, tunnel, handleHTTP and handleGRPC. connIdentity keeps the unverified sub and email that Verify returns for expired and invalid tokens, for the W-P1-BLOCK-02 deny check only; they never yield a Subject.
- HTTP/1.1 ORDER (the key requirement): in runRequestStages (internal/proxy/http.go) `stripHopHeaders` runs right after `readRequest` and deletes X-Warden-Identity. Capture the raw header value onto requestScope in a new `captureIdentityHeader(s)` called immediately BEFORE `stripHopHeaders` (more than one X-Warden-Identity value gives invalid/malformed), then add `identityStage` right after the strip and before `constraintGate` and `judgeGate`. The stage verifies the captured value, applies the status rules and sets `s.subject`. The raw value is never logged, never stored on an event and never passed to the judge, DLP or the MCP gateway.
- HTTP/2 and gRPC: no separate capture is needed. `serveGRPCStream` (internal/proxy/grpc.go) runs the SAME runRequestStages pipeline as HTTP/1.1 (#388), so the pre-strip `captureIdentityHeader` and `identityStage` in runRequestStages already cover h2 and gRPC streams (X-Warden-Identity is read from s.req.Header before stripHopHeaders deletes it). `copyGRPCHeaders` strips the same set on the upstream hop only after that, so the capture also runs before it. WebSocket upgrades, SSE and MCP requests are covered by the same pipeline. The proxy-only strip of h2 requests stays unchanged.
- Status rules (attribute mode never blocks): a CONNECT identity is re-checked against Expiry on every request (valid until exp plus skew, then expired); a header identity is used when CONNECT carried none; two valid identities with different sub give conflict and the request proceeds (a 403 identity_conflict is reserved for P2 require mode); a token sent in mode off gives off with NO Verify call; keys that cannot be fetched give unverified; no token gives none. Only valid yields a non-nil Subject on requestScope (`identity.SubjectFrom`).
- Exported constants in internal/proxy/identity.go: `IdentityHeader = "X-Warden-Identity"` and `ProxyAuthUsername = "session"` (the contract drift test in W-P1-IDC-01 and the identityclient env renderer pin their values; hopheaders.go keeps using the same header name).
- Transparent mode gap, stated and tested: transparent listeners (internal/proxy/transparent.go) have no CONNECT and no Proxy-Authorization, so they pass a zero connIdentity (status none); only X-Warden-Identity on terminated transparent traffic attributes, and raw transparent tunnels stay anonymous.
- Metrics: new nil-safe `(*Metrics).RecordIdentityVerify(result, reason)` in internal/observability registers the OTel counter `warden.identity.verify.total{result,reason}` with bounded labels (P2 extends this instrument, it does not add another); identity time is recorded with the existing `ObserveAddedLatency("identity", d)` (warden.request.added_latency, stage=identity). Budget: cached-token path under 100 us/op, measured with `testing.AllocsPerRun` plus a ns/op bound in a benchmark guard test.
- Startup warning: when mode is attribute and no CA is configured, log one warning that only CONNECT identity is available; also log one warning when the worker is transparent-only that only X-Warden-Identity can attribute. The raw token never reaches logs, events, the judge or the MCP gateway.
- Nothing here changes header stripping or CONNECT bounds. A CONNECT carrying a 16 KiB token in Proxy-Authorization must still be accepted (it fits the 64 KiB block), pinned by a new case.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add identityHolder, identityP, identity() and SetIdentity in internal/proxy/proxy.go, seeded from proxy.Config in New.
2. Add the new internal/proxy/identity.go with connIdentity, resolveConnIdentity(header value), captureIdentityHeader(s), resolveRequestIdentity(ci, raw) applying the status rules, and identityStage.
3. In internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn read Proxy-Authorization in the header loop, build connIdentity before Policy.EvaluateRequest and pass it to handleTLS and tunnel; in internal/proxy/tls.go pass it to handleHTTP and handleGRPC; transparent listeners pass the zero value.
4. Add connIdentity, rawIdentity and Subject fields to requestScope; in runRequestStages call captureIdentityHeader before stripHopHeaders and identityStage right after it (internal/proxy/http.go).
5. No grpc.go change is needed for the capture: serveGRPCStream calls runRequestStages, so step 3 covers h2 and gRPC. Only populate the requestScope identity inputs there if they are not already set by the shared pipeline (the connIdentity of the connection is passed down from handleTLS/handleGRPC into the h2 scope).
6. Add RecordIdentityVerify to internal/observability/observability.go and call it once per verification.
7. Tests: the new internal/proxy/identity_test.go (HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrade and h2/gRPC clients against a header-recording upstream, all modes, fakes.Verifier), TestIdentityHotSwap under -race, the transparent-mode case, and a benchmark/alloc guard next to http_bench_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Red first: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityCapturedBeforeStrip` fails if the capture is moved after `stripHopHeaders` (the verifier then sees no token and the status is none instead of valid), and passes with the capture ahead of the strip, for HTTP/1.1, a WebSocket upgrade and an h2/gRPC stream with X-Warden-Identity.
- [ ] Regression (the strip is on main): for HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrade and h2/gRPC, in mode off, with no settings and in attribute mode, the upstream never sees X-Warden-Identity or Proxy-Authorization: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestIdentityStripping|TestStripProxyHeaders'`.
- [ ] In mode off with a token present, fakes.Verifier records zero calls and the resolved status is off: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityModeOff`.
- [ ] In attribute mode, invalid, expired, missing, unverifiable and conflicting tokens are all forwarded (200 from upstream) with status invalid, expired, none, unverified and conflict, a nil Subject, and a matching warden.identity.verify.total increment: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityAttributeMode`.
- [ ] A CONNECT identity whose exp passes during a keep-alive session gives status valid on the first request and expired on a request after exp plus skew (fake clock): `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityConnectExpiry`.
- [ ] A CONNECT with two Proxy-Authorization lines, or a request with two X-Warden-Identity values, gives status invalid with reason malformed: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityDuplicateHeaders`.
- [ ] Transparent mode: a request through the transparent listener with X-Warden-Identity is attributed, one without it has status none, and no Proxy-Authorization is ever consulted: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityTransparent`.
- [ ] Concurrent SetIdentity swaps during traffic pass under `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityHotSwap`.
- [ ] A CONNECT carrying a 16 KiB token in Proxy-Authorization is accepted and attributed: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestConnectLargeProxyAuthorization`.
- [ ] The cached-token path stays under 100 us/op and allocates within the recorded bound: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityStageBudget` (uses testing.AllocsPerRun and a ns/op ceiling), and `go test ./internal/proxy -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkIdentityStage` runs.
- [ ] The startup warning is logged once for attribute mode without a CA and once for a transparent-only worker: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityStartupWarnings`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 3/12 · W-P1-VRFY-03

**Add identity fields to analytics.Event and the local SQLite store**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#23](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/23)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). Everything downstream (receipts, sync to the CP, the dashboard, policy replay) needs the user to be a first-class field on a recorded event. This ticket (#23) adds those fields to analytics.Event and to the worker's local SQLite store, including the GetOldestEventIDs read that feeds SyncWorker. It was split from the original M ticket #23: stamping the fields on every proxy event and decision log (the recordEvent chokepoint and emitDenyEventDetail) moved to W-P1-VRFY-09, because the storage work is separable from the proxy plumbing and lets W-P1-VRFY-06 (fleet store) start without the proxy change. It has no dependencies (no import of internal/identity or internal/proxy). Siblings: VRFY-09 (stamping), VRFY-06 (CP fleet store), VRFY-04 (user filter). Out of scope: the proxy, the decision log, the fleet store.

What to build: the Event fields with explicit snake_case json tags and omitempty (so unattributed events, receipts and sync payloads stay byte-identical, and old receipts keep verifying), the seven additive SQLite columns plus an index, and the JSON group helpers.

**Requirements**

- analytics.Event (internal/analytics/analytics.go) gains `UserSub, UserEmail string`, `UserGroups []string`, `UserGroupsTruncated bool`, `UserSID, IdentityStatus, IdentityReason string` with json tags `user_sub`, `user_email`, `user_groups`, `user_groups_truncated`, `user_sid`, `identity_status`, `identity_reason`, all omitempty. Existing field names and tags are unchanged. Exported helpers `EncodeGroups([]string) string` and `DecodeGroups(string) []string` (JSON array, never comma-joined) live in the analytics package so the fleet store (VRFY-06) reuses them.
- The local SQLiteStore adds the seven columns through addColumnIfAbsent (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' for strings, INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 for user_groups_truncated), plus an index on (user_sub, ts). user_groups is stored as a JSON array because LDAP DN group names contain commas.
- insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, the GetEvents scan, and the GetOldestEventIDs SELECT and scan all carry the new columns, so the fields reach SyncWorker and the CP. Round-trips keep a group such as `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` intact.
- Receipts cover the fields automatically, because SigningStore signs the marshalled Event. An identity-free Event marshals to exactly the same bytes as before, so old receipts keep verifying (internal/audit Receipt keeps the signed EventJSON bytes).
- No stamping logic here: nothing in internal/proxy changes. The fields are populated by W-P1-VRFY-09.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the fields and json tags to Event in internal/analytics/analytics.go, plus the exported EncodeGroups/DecodeGroups helpers.
2. Add the addColumnIfAbsent entries and the index in SQLiteStore migrate. Extend insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs.
3. Tests: a migration test from a fixture warden.db without the columns (pattern of activity_columns_test.go), a golden marshal test for an identity-free Event, an internal/audit receipt test, a SyncWorker test that reads the fields from GetOldestEventIDs, and a group round-trip test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An old warden.db with rows opens with the new columns added, old rows intact with defaults, and a second open is a no-op: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestMigrateUserColumns`.
- [ ] An identity-free Event marshals to the same bytes as before this change (golden file), and its receipt has no user_* keys. An attributed event's receipt contains "user_sub" and "identity_status":"valid" and audit.Verify passes: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestEventGoldenMarshal` and `go test ./internal/audit -run TestReceiptIdentityFields`.
- [ ] A group named `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` round-trips through StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs unchanged: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestUserGroupsRoundTrip`.
- [ ] SyncWorker sends the user fields read from GetOldestEventIDs to an ingest endpoint: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestSyncWorkerCarriesIdentity`.
- [ ] The migration, golden and round-trip tests fail (red first) before the fields exist; `git diff --stat origin/main -- internal/proxy` is empty.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 4/12 · W-P1-VRFY-04

**Add the user filter to the event stores and the traffic and analytics APIs**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#24](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/24)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). Once events carry the user (W-P1-VRFY-03 locally, W-P1-VRFY-06 on the CP), operators need to filter by user. This ticket (#24) adds `EventFilter.User` to the local, central and fleet stores and exposes `?user=` on the traffic and analytics APIs on worker and CP dashboards, including the analytics cache key. It was split from the original M ticket #24: the top-users table and the UI user column and filter box moved to W-P1-VRFY-10, so API consumers (W-P4-AMCP-01, W-P3-PUL-05, the L2 smoke W-P1-IDC-03 polling `?user=`) depend only on this smaller part. It depends on VRFY-03 and VRFY-06 (columns on both stores). Out of scope: topUsers aggregate and UI (VRFY-10). The Query Builder needs no code change: its schema already comes from PRAGMA table_info, so the user columns appear there; only a test covers it.

What to build: the filter, the query parameter with its bound, the cache-key change, with parameterized SQL only.

**Requirements**

- analytics.EventFilter gains `User`, matching user_sub exactly or `lower(user_email) = lower(User)`, with parameterized SQL only (no string-built SQL). SQLiteStore, CentralStore and FleetSQLiteStore honor it (AggregatedFilter through embedding). The filter uses the (user_sub, ts) index.
- /dashboard/api/traffic and /dashboard/api/analytics accept `?user=` (at most 320 characters, otherwise 400 `{"error":...}`). The value is normalized (trimmed) before use. The handleAnalytics cache key includes the normalized user value so one user's figures are never served for another.
- The Query Builder needs no change: GET /dashboard/api/query/schema lists user_sub and user_email, and a POST /dashboard/api/query with `SELECT user_sub, count(*) FROM events GROUP BY user_sub` returns rows; this is covered by a test only.
- With no `user` parameter responses are unchanged byte for byte. This ticket adds no routes (the existing handlers gain a parameter), so rule X9 is unaffected.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add User to EventFilter in internal/analytics/analytics.go and apply it in SQLiteStore.GetEvents, CentralStore.GetEvents/GetAggregatedEvents (internal/analytics/central.go) and FleetSQLiteStore.GetEvents/GetAggregatedEvents (internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go).
2. In internal/dashboard/dashboard.go, parse and bound ?user= in handleTraffic and handleAnalytics, and add the normalized user to the analytics cache key (currently range + proxy).
3. Tests in internal/analytics (filter on all three stores, SQL injection attempt as a literal) and internal/dashboard/dashboard_test.go (parameter, bound, cache key, schema).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With events for alice@corp and bob@corp in local and fleet stores, GET /dashboard/api/traffic?user=Alice@Corp returns 200 with only Alice's events on worker and CP, and ?user=<alice-sub> returns the same set: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestTrafficUserFilter`.
- [ ] After /dashboard/api/analytics?range=24h&user=alice is cached, the same call with user=bob returns Bob's figures: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestAnalyticsUserCacheKey`.
- [ ] ?user= longer than 320 characters returns 400: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestUserParamBound`.
- [ ] `?user=x' OR '1'='1` matches nothing and returns 200 (parameterized): `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestUserFilterIsParameterized`.
- [ ] GET /dashboard/api/query/schema lists user_sub and user_email, and POST /dashboard/api/query with `SELECT user_sub, count(*) FROM events GROUP BY user_sub` returns 200 with rows: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestQueryBuilderUserColumns`.
- [ ] Without `user`, the traffic and analytics responses are unchanged: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/analytics`.

### 5/12 · W-P1-VRFY-05

**Add identity attribution scenarios on the L1 harness**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#25](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/25)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). This ticket (#25) proves attribution end to end, in process: a real worker and control plane boot on loopback through test/harness, the issuer is the in-process fake from W-P1-VRFY-11, and the harness's fake upstream records what arrives. It is a set of L1 scenarios (test/scenarios), not a test/integration rig and not a Docker test; CI needs no Docker. The original ticket also asked for a Dex branch behind WARDEN_IT_DEX and a new CI integration job. Both are dropped: CI already runs `scripts/check.sh --integration` (.github/workflows/ci.yml, job runs `scripts/check.sh --integration --json-out check-report.json`), `test/integration` holds only TestSingleBinary, and real Dex coverage is the L2 smoke W-P1-IDC-03. The issuer fake and agent token helpers moved to W-P1-VRFY-11 so later features can depend on them alone. Depends on VRFY-07 (a worker that actually verifies), VRFY-09 (stamping on events) and VRFY-11 (the fake). Out of scope: Dex, Docker, the fake itself.

What to build: a `harness.WithIdentity` option that turns on attribute mode with the fake issuer, and the scenario table.

**Requirements**

- New option `harness.WithIdentity(mode string)` in test/harness: it adds an `identity` block to the worker policy (issuer = the fake's URL, audience `warden`, allowedAZP [agent-harness, warden-cli], `internalIssuerURL` set to the fake's own origin, a no-op rewrite that satisfies the http-issuer rule of W-P1-VRFY-12 for the loopback http issuer) with the given default mode, and implies `WithOIDCIssuer()`.
- New file test/scenarios/identity.go registered in scenarios_list.go; scenario names start with `identity_` so `go test ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/identity_'` selects them. L2 is false (they use the in-process issuer).
- Cases, each via `Proxy-Authorization` on CONNECT (`AgentWithProxyToken`) and via `X-Warden-Identity` (request header, over a CA-enabled worker), over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (`AgentH2WithProxyToken`): valid, expired, wrong audience, wrong azp and missing token. Plus one raw-tunnel case (CONNECT identity only), one conflict case (two valid tokens with different sub), one mode-off case (token sent, identity_status off, no Verify call) and one case with the issuer stopped and a cold cache (status unverified, request still succeeds).
- Oracles: `h.Events()` (user_sub, user_email, user_groups, identity_status, identity_reason; no user fields for invalid or expired tokens), `h.Upstream(host).Requests()` (neither Proxy-Authorization nor X-Warden-Identity ever arrives), `h.Metrics()` (warden.identity.verify.total count per result and reason), `h.Logs()` (no token string anywhere) and the JSON an event signs (the receipt body carries user_sub for the valid case).
- Every request returns the upstream's 200 in attribute mode; a deny caused by policy (non-allowlisted host) with a valid token is attributed (deny event with user_sub and status valid).
- Transparent mode (#376) is covered by one scenario using `h.TransparentAgent()`: only `X-Warden-Identity` attributes, and the no-header case records status none. Output never prints token strings.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add harness.WithIdentity in test/harness (reusing the W-P1-VRFY-11 issuer) and a harness test that the worker boots with it.
2. Write test/scenarios/identity.go with the case table and register each scenario in scenarios_list.go.
3. Run `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/identity_'`, then the whole `go test ./test/scenarios`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] All cases return the upstream's 200 and the events carry IdentityStatus valid, expired, invalid, none, conflict, off or unverified as expected: `go test -race ./test/scenarios -run 'TestScenarios/identity_'`. The valid-token cases fail (red first) when VRFY-09 stamping is removed.
- [ ] No subtest observes Proxy-Authorization or X-Warden-Identity at the upstream, in any mode, including mode off.
- [ ] warden.identity.verify.total shows the expected count for each result and reason after the run (read through h.Metrics(), guarded by h.MetricsAvailable()).
- [ ] No raw token or password appears in h.Logs() or in the captured test output: the scenario asserts it.
- [ ] The issuer-stopped case yields identity_status unverified with reason jwks_unavailable and a successful request.
- [ ] Transparent scenario: `X-Warden-Identity` attributes and a missing header records none, with no Proxy-Authorization consulted.
- [ ] `go vet ./test/...` is clean, `go test ./test/harness` passes, and `scripts/check.sh --integration` stays green (no new integration file is added).

**Store user fields in the control-plane fleet store**

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). Control-plane half of recording (#228): the fleet store behind the CP dashboard must keep the user fields that workers sync (W-P1-VRFY-03 defines the Event fields and the exported EncodeGroups/DecodeGroups helpers). ### 7/12 · W-P1-VRFY-07

**Wire the identity verifier into worker assembly, hot reload and deployment**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#229](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/229)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). Connects the verifier to real workers (#229): build it from local config or the distributed SettingsWire, resolve the per-agent mode with the agent ID that worker.defaultAgentID (internal/worker/judge.go) already computes, and swap it through SettingsApplier (internal/worker/applier.go) without a restart. It also opens worker egress to the issuer in the deploy templates and documents the identity block, the transport rules and the rollout order. Mode stays off unless configured. Depends on VRFY-01 (NewOIDCVerifier), VRFY-02 (SetIdentity and the proxy side) and VRFY-08 (IdentitySettings). Siblings: VRFY-05 (L1 scenarios), the L2 smoke W-P1-IDC-03. Out of scope: the proxy extraction (VRFY-02), config types (VRFY-08).

**Requirements**

- Worker assembly (internal/worker/worker.go) builds the verifier from pol.Identity and calls proxy SetIdentity. The mode comes from the matching Agents entry's Identity, then Identity.DefaultMode, then off, keyed by defaultAgentID.
- SettingsApplier.Apply rebuilds the verifier only when issuer, internalIssuerURL, audience, JWKS URL, azp, skew or TTL settings change. Otherwise it only updates the mode.
- A rebuild failure, or an unknown mode from a newer CP, keeps the previous identity config and logs one warning without token data.
- deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml and the compose templates allow worker egress to the issuer, documented as an operator-set value.
- docs/control-plane.md documents the identity block, the per-agent Identity field, the rule that X-Warden-Identity needs TLS termination while Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT works everywhere, the rule that sub is authoritative and email matching needs a verified email, the recommended `allowedAZP: [agent-harness, warden-cli]` for the reference Dex clients, and the CP-first rollout order.
- Worker startup never contacts the issuer, so a worker with Dex down still starts.
- docs/control-plane.md also states the limits and the gaps plainly: a token is at most 16 KiB; the CONNECT request line is capped at 8 KiB and the header block at 64 KiB with a 10 s deadline (431, deny reason malformed_connect, detail headers_too_large); in transparent mode (#376) there is no CONNECT, so only X-Warden-Identity on terminated traffic attributes; and a P1 identity is a bearer assertion signed by the IdP and not yet bound to the agent (P2 adds binding and bundle-distributed JWKS).
- Worker assembly lives in internal/worker (data-plane assembly) and adds no route and no new package, so architecture.yaml needs no change; the new import of internal/identity must be allowed by the layer rules (assembly may import everything).
- The verifier config is built from IdentitySettings including `internalIssuerURL` (passed as identity.Config.InternalIssuerURL), so a worker container reaches an IdP on the compose network while the issuer stays public; a rebuild happens when it changes (add it to the list in the SettingsApplier rule above).

**Implementation plan**

1. In internal/worker/worker.go, build the verifier with identity.NewOIDCVerifier and resolve the mode using defaultAgentID (internal/worker/judge.go).
2. In internal/worker/applier.go, compare the previous and new identity settings, then rebuild or update the mode and call SetIdentity.
3. Update deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml and the compose templates under deploy/compose for issuer egress.
4. Update docs/control-plane.md.
5. Tests in internal/worker/applier_test.go and a worker assembly test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a SettingsWire whose Agents entry for this worker sets Identity=attribute and DefaultMode off, Apply activates verification without a restart: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestSettingsApplierIdentity`.
- [ ] An Apply that changes only an unrelated setting keeps the same verifier instance, and an issuer change replaces it.
- [ ] An unknown mode keeps the previous config and logs one warning.
- [ ] A worker configured with an unreachable issuer starts and serves traffic in its test.
- [ ] A worker built from a local `identity:` block (no CP) attributes with the mode from its Agents entry, and a worker whose served settings carry mode `require` (unknown to P1) keeps the previous config: `go test ./internal/worker -run 'TestWorkerLocalIdentity|TestSettingsApplierIdentityUnknownMode'`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including any manifest validation.
- [ ] `grep -E '16 KiB|8 KiB|64 KiB|transparent' docs/control-plane.md` matches the new identity section, and `grep -E '32 KiB|100 lines' docs/control-plane.md` prints nothing.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-01`](identity-verification.md#112--w-p1-vrfy-01) Add internal/identity OIDC verifier with lazy JWKS, cache and config; [`W-P1-VRFY-02`](identity-verification.md#212--w-p1-vrfy-02) Extract and verify identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 before the proxy-only strip; [`W-P1-VRFY-08`](identity-verification.md#812--w-p1-vrfy-08) Add the identity settings block to SettingsWire, local YAML and the per-agent field

### 8/12 · W-P1-VRFY-08

**Add the identity settings block to SettingsWire, local YAML and the per-agent field**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#440](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/440)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). A worker needs to be told which issuer to trust and which agents attribute. This ticket adds that configuration end to end and nothing else: the `identity` settings block on the CP-to-worker wire (SettingsWire), the same block in a standalone worker's local YAML, the per-agent `identity` mode field, validation, and the CP settings writer so a dashboard edit never drops the block. It was split from the original M ticket #21 (W-P1-VRFY-01, the verifier package) because config and the verifier are separate subsystems with different consumers: p1-group-policy, p2 binding and the docs need the keys, not the verifier. It has no dependencies and needs no import of internal/identity (the mode strings are constants in internal/config). Siblings: VRFY-01 (the verifier that reads this config), VRFY-07 (builds the verifier from this config on the worker and hot-reloads it), VRFY-02 (uses the resolved mode). Out of scope: building a verifier, hot reload, deploy templates, docs (VRFY-07).

What to build: IdentitySettings and its YAML/JSON plumbing in internal/config, per-agent mode, validation, and the CP writer. With no `identity` block everything behaves as today (mode off).

**Requirements**

- New internal/config/identity.go: `IdentitySettings{DefaultMode, Issuer, Audience string; AllowedAZP []string; JWKSURL, GroupsClaim string; ClockSkewSeconds, MaxTokenTTLSeconds int; InternalIssuerURL string}` with json and yaml keys `defaultMode`, `issuer`, `audience`, `allowedAZP`, `jwksURL`, `groupsClaim`, `clockSkewSeconds`, `maxTokenTTLSeconds`, `internalIssuerURL` (optional; the origin containers use to reach the issuer, for example `http://dex:5556`; there is no insecure-issuer key); mode constants `IdentityModeOff = "off"` and `IdentityModeAttribute = "attribute"`; `validateIdentity`. allowedAZP has no built-in default (empty means no azp check); reference configs and docs set [agent-harness, warden-cli]. The block holds no secrets.
- `SettingsWire.Identity *IdentitySettings` (json `identity`, omitempty; absent means off) in internal/config/settings.go. Extend `SettingsWire.DeepCopy` (including AllowedAZP and InternalIssuerURL) and `SettingsWireFromPolicy`, and add the reverse projection used by the worker, so the block round-trips byte-identically and a SettingsWire without it marshals with no `identity` key.
- Local YAML: a top-level `identity:` block parsed through rawConfig under KnownFields(true) into a new `Policy.Identity` field, so standalone workers and the CP-served copy both parse it.
- Per-agent override: a new `Identity string` field on `AgentSettings` (json `identity`, omitempty), `AgentPolicy` and `rawAgent` (yaml `identity`), keeping the existing `AgentSettings(a)` conversion in SettingsWireFromPolicy compiling. `validateAgents` accepts only "", off or attribute for it.
- Validation (local YAML and the CP write path): modes are off|attribute; `require` is rejected with an error containing "Phase 2"; an unknown mode is rejected; issuer and audience are required when any mode other than off is set; an `http://` issuer is rejected unless `internalIssuerURL` is set (the same rule as identity.CheckIssuer of W-P1-VRFY-12, applied here without importing internal/identity: https always passes, plain http only with an internal issuer URL); `internalIssuerURL` is optional and, when set, must be an absolute http or https URL with an empty path or `/`, no userinfo, query or fragment, and is accepted only together with a non-empty issuer; clockSkewSeconds is 0..300 (0 means the default 60) and maxTokenTTLSeconds > 0 means an override of the default 3600. `parseRemotePolicy` on a worker does NOT reject a served wire carrying an unsupported mode, so a later CP never stalls a P1 worker; W-P1-VRFY-07 keeps the previous identity config in that case.
- CP settings writer: `controlplane.Server.WriteSettings` (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) gets an `identity` entry in its settingsBlocks table that encodes in.Identity into the on-disk `identity:` block (or removes it when nil), and `agentYAML` / `agentsSettingsNode` carry the per-agent `identity` key, so a dashboard settings edit round-trips the block and the per-agent field. The other writers (WritePolicy, WriteIntegrations, WriteDetection) leave the block byte-identical.
- Wire hygiene: the block is secret-free; the existing TestPolicyServedExcludesSecrets and TestPolicyIncludesSettingsAndETagCovers keep passing, and the served ETag covers the identity block.
- Back-compat: a config with no `identity` block and no per-agent field parses and serves exactly as before.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first: internal/config/identity_test.go (validation table, YAML parse) and the round-trip cases in internal/config/settings_test.go.
2. Add internal/config/identity.go; add the Identity field to Policy/rawConfig in internal/config/config.go and call validateIdentity from validate().
3. Add Identity to SettingsWire, AgentSettings, AgentPolicy and rawAgent; extend SettingsWireFromPolicy, the reverse projection and SettingsWire.DeepCopy in internal/config/settings.go; extend validateAgents in internal/config/agents.go.
4. In internal/controlplane/controlplane.go add the `identity` blockEdit and the per-agent key to agentYAML/agentsSettingsNode; add TestWriteSettingsIdentity and extend the writers-preserve test.
5. Add a commented identity example to configs/config.control-plane.yaml and configs/config.example-worker.yaml (issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex`, `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` marked dev-only split-horizon, audience warden, allowedAZP [agent-harness, warden-cli]); the production example shows an https issuer and no internalIssuerURL.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A SettingsWire with an identity block and per-agent Identity round-trips byte-identically through marshal, unmarshal and DeepCopy, and a SettingsWire without one marshals with no `identity` key: `go test ./internal/config -run 'Identity'`.
- [ ] Mode `require` fails with a message containing `Phase 2`; an unknown mode fails; an http issuer without `internalIssuerURL` fails and with `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` passes; an https issuer passes with or without it; an internalIssuerURL with a path (`http://dex:5556/dex`), a query, a non-http scheme, or set with an empty issuer fails; a missing issuer or audience fails when a mode is attribute: `go test ./internal/config -run TestValidateIdentity`.
- [ ] `parseRemotePolicy` on a served wire with mode `require` returns the policy without error: `go test ./internal/config -run TestRemotePolicyUnknownIdentityMode`.
- [ ] A dashboard-style WriteSettings with an identity block and a per-agent identity writes both to the YAML, and WritePolicy, WriteIntegrations and WriteDetection leave the identity node byte-identical: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWriteSettingsIdentity|TestWritersPreserveIdentityBlock'`.
- [ ] The served /policy JSON contains the identity block under `settings` and the ETag changes when it changes: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyServedIncludesIdentity`.
- [ ] A config with no identity block parses and serves unchanged: `go test ./internal/config ./internal/controlplane`.
- [ ] `grep -rniE 'allowInsecure[I]ssuer' internal/config configs` prints nothing, and a config that still sets the removed insecure-issuer key (the old `allowInsecure` + `Issuer` spelling) is rejected by the strict (KnownFields) parser: `go test ./internal/config -run TestIdentityNoInsecureKey`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-IDC-01`](identity-contract.md#17--w-p1-idc-01) Write the agent identity contract for harness builders; [`W-P1-DEX-03`](dex-oidc.md#36--w-p1-dex-03) Document Dex as Warden's IdP with connector, failure-mode and prod guidance; [`W-P1-VRFY-07`](identity-verification.md#712--w-p1-vrfy-07) Wire the identity verifier into worker assembly, hot reload and deployment

### 9/12 · W-P1-VRFY-09

**Stamp identity on every proxy event and decision log**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#441](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/441)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). W-P1-VRFY-02 resolves who the caller is (connIdentity) and W-P1-VRFY-03 gave events and the store identity fields; this ticket connects them: every analytics event the proxy writes carries the caller's identity, and every decision log line names the user and status. It was split from the original M ticket #23 (the Event and storage half stayed in W-P1-VRFY-03). It depends on VRFY-02 (connIdentity) and VRFY-03 (fields). Siblings: VRFY-05 (L1 scenarios that assert the stamping end to end), VRFY-06/04 (CP side). Out of scope: columns and Event fields (VRFY-03), identity resolution (VRFY-02).

What to build: one chokepoint `p.recordEvent(ci connIdentity, e analytics.Event)` that stamps identity, used by every store call in the proxy, including the deny chokepoint `emitDenyEventDetail`, plus decisionLog fields, plus an AST test that keeps it that way.

**Requirements**

- New `(ci connIdentity) stamp(ev *analytics.Event)` and `(p *Proxy) recordEvent(ci connIdentity, ev analytics.Event)` in internal/proxy/identity.go. stamp writes IdentityStatus and IdentityReason whenever the status is set (a zero connIdentity, and mode off with no token, leave the event byte-identical to today); it writes UserSub, UserEmail, UserGroups, UserGroupsTruncated and UserSID ONLY when status is valid. Unverified claims of an expired or invalid token are never written onto an event.
- Replace every direct `p.analyticsStore().StoreEvent(...)` call in internal/proxy with recordEvent. Sites on main: internal/proxy/secretscope.go:85, serve.go:390, ws.go:193, tls.go:98, tls.go:215, http.go:1257, http.go:1423 and deny.go:96 (`emitDenyEventDetail`). internal/proxy/grpc.go has no direct StoreEvent call (it records through the shared paths).
- The deny chokepoint is the important one: change `emitDenyEvent(ev)` and `emitDenyEventDetail(ev, detail)` to take the connIdentity (`emitDenyEvent(ci, ev)`), have `emitDeny(s, ...)` pass the scope's identity, and give `storeDeny` a `ci` parameter; pre-CONNECT parse failures (malformed request line, preamble limits) pass the zero connIdentity. Stamp once inside emitDenyEventDetail so no deny caller stamps by hand, and so a CONNECT deny with a valid Proxy-Authorization token is attributed.
- decisionLog (internal/proxy/observe.go) gains user_sub (valid only), identity_status, identity_reason and groups_count, emitted only when set. Email and the group list are logged only at debug level, and the token never.
- AST test `TestAllEventsCarryIdentity` in internal/proxy: fails if any non-test file in the package calls StoreEvent outside recordEvent (the same pattern as the repo's other AST guards).
- Transparent mode and raw tunnels pass the zero value or the CONNECT identity unchanged; nothing here adds a Verify call.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add recordEvent and stamp in internal/proxy/identity.go with table tests first.
2. Replace each direct StoreEvent call listed above; thread the connIdentity through emitDeny, emitDenyEvent, emitDenyEventDetail and storeDeny (zero value at the pre-CONNECT sites).
3. Extend decisionLog and logDecision in internal/proxy/observe.go.
4. Add the AST test and the behaviour tests with fakes.Verifier and the FakeAnalyticsStore.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Red first: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestAllEventsCarryIdentity` fails while any non-test file calls StoreEvent outside recordEvent, and passes after the replacement.
- [ ] A CONNECT to a denied host with a valid Proxy-Authorization token stores a deny event with the user's sub and identity_status valid: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestDenyEventCarriesIdentity`.
- [ ] An allowed request, a secret-scope deny, a WebSocket event and an h2 event each carry the same identity fields: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestEventsCarryIdentityAllPaths`.
- [ ] An expired or invalid token stores identity_status and identity_reason but no user_sub, user_email or user_groups: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestUnverifiedClaimsNotRecorded`.
- [ ] With no identity configured, stored events are identical to before (no user_* or identity_* values): `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestNoIdentityEventsUnchanged`.
- [ ] Captured decision log output contains user_sub and identity_status for an attributed request and never the raw token or the email: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestDecisionLogIdentity`.

### 10/12 · W-P1-VRFY-10

**Add the top-users breakdown and the user column and filter box to the dashboard**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#442](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/442)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). W-P1-VRFY-04 (#24) added the `?user=` filter on the APIs; this ticket shows it to operators. It adds a `topUsers` block to the analytics response and, in the dashboard UI, a user column on the traffic table and a filter box that sets `?user=`. It was split from the original M ticket #24 so the API part (VRFY-04) can merge and be consumed alone. It depends on VRFY-04. W-P1-BLOCK-04 builds its block-user links on the user rows rendered here. Out of scope: the filter itself (VRFY-04), any new route, per-user usage and cost (W-P3-PUL-05).

What to build: the topUsers aggregate on worker and fleet stores and the HTML/JS changes in internal/dashboard/index.html. Claim values come from an IdP, so they are rendered as text only.

**Requirements**

- Analytics computation adds `topUsers`: the top 10 users by request count with their deny count, grouped by user_sub with the latest user_email for display, plus exactly one `unattributed` bucket for events with an empty user_sub, sorted by count descending. It is computed for both the worker store and the fleet store (CP) in the same analytics handler (internal/dashboard and the store aggregations in internal/analytics).
- With no identity data in the store, the analytics response is unchanged apart from an empty `topUsers` list (and the unattributed bucket may be omitted when it is the only bucket and holds every event: state the choice in the test).
- internal/dashboard/index.html: a user column in the traffic table (email, falling back to sub), a filter box that sets `?user=` on the traffic and analytics calls (bounded to 320 characters client-side), and a top-users table. Claim values (email, sub, group names) are rendered with textContent only, never innerHTML.
- The Query Builder needs no change. No new route is added, so rule X9 is unaffected.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the topUsers aggregate to the analytics computation for the worker store and FleetSQLiteStore, with store-level tests first.
2. Expose topUsers in the /dashboard/api/analytics response in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go.
3. Add the user column, filter box and top-users table to internal/dashboard/index.html.
4. Tests in internal/dashboard (handler output, served HTML) and internal/analytics (aggregate).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] topUsers has at most 10 entries sorted by count descending, one `unattributed` bucket, and ties are broken by sub for a stable order: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestTopUsers` and `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestAnalyticsTopUsers`.
- [ ] With no identity data, GET /dashboard/api/analytics returns an empty topUsers list and every other field is unchanged: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestAnalyticsNoIdentity`.
- [ ] The served index.html contains the user filter input and the `?user=` wiring, and no claim-derived value reaches innerHTML (a Go test over the served HTML fails if `innerHTML` is assigned from user_email, user_sub or group fields): `go test ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestIndexUserFilterPresent|TestIndexRendersClaimsAsText'`. The second test fails (red first) when a user field is concatenated into innerHTML.
- [ ] On the CP (fleet store) and on a worker the same request returns the same shape: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestTopUsersWorkerAndFleet`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 11/12 · W-P1-VRFY-11

**Add the in-process OIDC issuer fake and agent token options to the test harness**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#443](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/443)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). Attribution scenarios (W-P1-VRFY-05) and several later features (block list, group policy, token exchange, per-user limits, offboarding, security tests) need a controllable OIDC issuer without Docker. This ticket was split out of the original scenario ticket #25 (W-P1-VRFY-05) so those features depend on the fake alone. It provides: an in-process OIDC issuer fake and the harness plumbing to send tokens from the agent. It depends on VRFY-01 only for a conformance test against the real verifier (the verifier-seam suite identitytest.RunVerifierSuite of VRFY-01 is separate and is not extended here). Out of scope: the scenarios themselves and the worker identity option (VRFY-05), real Dex (p1-dex).

What to build: `fakes.OIDCIssuer` in test/fakes, harness helpers that let the agent present a token, and a conformance test.

**Requirements**

- New `test/fakes/oidcissuer.go`: `fakes.OIDCIssuer`, an httptest server serving `/.well-known/openid-configuration` and a JWKS endpoint, started with `fakes.NewOIDCIssuer(tb, opts...)`, `Issuer() string`, `Stop()` / `Start()` (issuer-down and cold-cache cases) and a JWKS request counter. Keys are generated per instance (RS256 and ES256); NO private key is committed. `Mint(opts ...MintOption) string` signs a token with overrides for any claim (iss, sub, aud, azp, email, email_verified, groups, sid, exp, nbf, iat, nonce), the alg, kid, signing key and extra header fields; convenience constructors `Valid(sub, email, groups...)`, `Expired()`, `WrongAudience()`, `WrongAZP()`, `TooLong()` (exp-iat over 1h) and `RotateKey()` which adds a key with a new kid and signs with it. These names are the API W-P2-SECT-01 later extends, so keep them stable.
- test/fakes/oidcissuer.go must not import internal/controlplane or internal/identity (the rule is scoped to this file: fakes.Verifier from W-P1-VRFY-01 legitimately imports internal/identity; no dependency cycle, and the fake must not share code with the code under test). It uses only the standard library plus an existing JWT-free signer built on crypto/rsa and crypto/ecdsa (no new go.mod dependency). (test files may import internal/identity/identitytest: the shared verifier suite from W-P1-VRFY-01 runs from test/fakes/verifier_test.go).
- test/harness: `h.AgentWithProxyToken(token) *http.Client` and `h.AgentH2WithProxyToken(token) *http.Client` (the same transport as Agent/AgentH2, proxy URL `http://session:<token>@<worker>`, so Go sends `Proxy-Authorization: Basic` on CONNECT) and `h.ConnectStatusWithAuth(hostPort, proxyAuthorization string) int` for raw CONNECT cases (Bearer form, malformed form, duplicate lines). Per-request `X-Warden-Identity` needs no helper: a scenario sets the header on its request. Add the option `harness.WithOIDCIssuer()` that starts the fake for the scenario and exposes it as `h.Issuer()`; it stops at cleanup.
- Conformance test in test/harness (it may import internal/identity): `TestOIDCIssuerConformance` verifies every Mint variant against the real `identity.NewOIDCVerifier` and expects valid, expired, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, ttl_too_long, rotated kid (one JWKS refetch) and issuer stopped with a cold cache (`unverified`, `jwks_unavailable`). Unit tests of the fake itself live in test/fakes.
- No token is ever logged by the fake or the helpers; failures print claim names, not token strings.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write test/fakes/oidcissuer_test.go first (discovery document shape, JWKS contents, Mint claim overrides, RotateKey, Stop/Start, counter), then the fake.
2. Add the harness helpers and WithOIDCIssuer option in test/harness; add TestOIDCIssuerConformance.
3. Document the fake in test/scenarios/README.md (one paragraph: how to mint tokens in a scenario).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./test/fakes -run TestOIDCIssuer` passes: discovery and JWKS are served, Mint honors every override, RotateKey publishes a second kid, Stop makes the JWKS endpoint unreachable and Start restores it.
- [ ] `go test ./test/harness -run TestOIDCIssuerConformance` passes against the real verifier for valid, expired, wrong audience, wrong azp, over-long lifetime, rotated key and stopped issuer (red first: it fails before the fake exists).
- [ ] `go test ./test/harness -run TestAgentWithProxyToken` shows a header-recording CONNECT listener receives `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` from both agent clients.
- [ ] `oidcissuer.go` imports only the standard library, never `internal/identity` or `internal/controlplane`: `go test ./test/fakes -run TestOIDCIssuerFileImportsNeitherIdentityNorControlPlane` passes. (Scoped to the file: the package as a whole imports `internal/identity` through `fakes.Verifier` from W-P1-VRFY-01, so a package-wide `go list -deps` check cannot pass.)
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.
