### 12/12 · W-P1-VRFY-12

**Add the shared OIDC HTTP client with internal-origin rewrite and the http-issuer rule**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#444](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/444)

Context: feature p1-verify-token (epic #20). Every server-side OIDC call in Warden must work in the dev and demo setup, where the browser and the CLI on the host reach the IdP at `http://localhost:5556/dex` while containers (the CP and the workers) cannot: inside a container `localhost` is the container itself, and the IdP is reachable only as `http://dex:5556` on the compose network. The decision is split-horizon: the issuer string stays the public one (`http://localhost:5556/dex`, byte-identical in every token, discovery document and redirect), and containers that must call the IdP set an optional internal issuer URL (for example `http://dex:5556`). Server-side calls (discovery, JWKS, token exchange) whose origin equals the issuer's origin are sent to the internal origin; only the scheme, host and port of the TCP destination change, so go-oidc's issuer checks still pass. This ticket (new, created by the Dex-learnings pass; no GitHub issue yet) is the shared foundation: one dedicated `http.Client` with that rewrite, the way to hand it to go-oidc and golang.org/x/oauth2, and the http-issuer rule. It creates the package internal/identity (the scaffold; the verifier arrives in W-P1-VRFY-01) and adds the go-oidc and golang.org/x/oauth2 dependencies. Siblings: W-P1-VRFY-01 (the verifier; depends on this ticket and builds no client of its own), W-P1-VRFY-08 (worker `identity.internalIssuerURL` key), W-P1-SSO-02 (console `console.oidc.internalIssuerURL` key), W-P1-SSO-03 (console login: discovery and code exchange use this client), W-P1-DEX-01/02/04 (dev issuer and container configs). Out of scope here: the verifier, config parsing and validation of the YAML keys, wiring into the worker or CP, the Dex files and docs.

What to build: the client constructor with the origin-only rewrite, the context helper that hands the client to go-oidc and oauth2, and the http-issuer rule, all with network-free unit tests (httptest servers). Architecture gate: every new package needs exactly one class in architecture.yaml (rule L8) and a zone (Z1); every new third-party module needs an entry in the S3 `modules:` manifest of architecture.yaml. Run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` after editing architecture.yaml.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- New package internal/identity (new files `doc.go` and `httpclient.go`, plus `httpclient_test.go`). Add `internal/identity` to architecture.yaml with exactly one class (it performs network I/O, so not the `domain` class) and a zone (Z1), and add `github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3` and `golang.org/x/oauth2` (and any direct dependency go.mod then lists as direct) to the S3 `modules:` manifest with the layers that import them (internal/identity now; the control-plane assembly later); run `go run ./cmd/archgen`. Both modules are pinned to exact versions at least two weeks old; govulncheck stays clean. No route, no other package.
- `type HTTPClientConfig struct{ Issuer, InternalIssuerURL, CAFile string }` and `NewHTTPClient(cfg HTTPClientConfig) (*http.Client, error)`. It calls CheckIssuer first and returns its error. The client has Proxy=nil (the environment proxy is never used), a plain `net.Dialer` and not the proxy SafeDialer (so an IdP on a private network such as Dex on cp-net is reachable, like newControlPlaneHTTPClient in internal/worker/wiring.go), an overall timeout of 5s, a response body capped at 1 MiB (a longer body fails the read), no redirect following (CheckRedirect returns http.ErrUseLastResponse), TLS 1.2 minimum and an optional CAFile as RootCAs. Construction does no network I/O. These limits live here and only here: W-P1-VRFY-01 and W-P1-SSO-03 do not build their own client.
- Internal-origin rewrite, implemented as an `http.RoundTripper` wrapped around the transport and not in `DialContext`. Reason: only a RoundTripper can change the scheme (an internal `http://dex:5556` behind a public `https://` issuer, or the reverse) as well as host and port, and it sees the full request URL; a DialContext only sees `host:port`. For a request whose origin equals the issuer's origin (lower-cased scheme and host, port with the default 80/443 filled in) it clones the request (the caller's *http.Request is never mutated), sets URL.Scheme and URL.Host from InternalIssuerURL and sets `Host` to the original URL host, so the Host header, URL path and query, every other header, the body, the issuer string and every claim stay byte-identical. A request for any other origin (for example a jwks_uri on another host) passes through untouched. With an empty InternalIssuerURL the client rewrites nothing. Because redirects are not followed, a response can never move a request to another origin.
- `CheckIssuer(issuer, internalIssuerURL string) error` is the http-issuer rule and the only place it lives (W-P1-VRFY-08 and W-P1-SSO-02 apply the same rule to their config keys). The issuer must be an absolute http or https URL with a host and no userinfo, query or fragment. An https issuer is always accepted. A plain-http issuer is accepted only when internalIssuerURL is set (the dev profile: the operator opted into a split-horizon setup); otherwise it fails with an error that names `internalIssuerURL` and says https is required. internalIssuerURL, when set, must be an absolute http or https URL with an empty path or `/`, no userinfo, query or fragment, and requires a non-empty issuer. There is no insecure flag, no loopback exception and no environment override anywhere in the package. Fail closed: any parse problem is an error, never a silent acceptance.
- `WithHTTPClient(ctx context.Context, c *http.Client) context.Context` sets BOTH `oidc.ClientContext(ctx, c)` (go-oidc discovery and JWKS) and `context.WithValue(ctx, oauth2.HTTPClient, c)` (oauth2 `Exchange` and `Refresh`), so discovery, JWKS and the code exchange all use the one client. Its godoc states that every go-oidc and oauth2 call must receive a context made through it, and that a context given to `oidc.NewRemoteKeySet` outlives the call, so it must not be a request context.
- No token, code or response body is ever logged or placed in an error by this package; errors wrap the transport error only. The package imports no Dex-specific identifier or URL (the neutrality guard of W-P1-VRFY-01 covers it).
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/identity/httpclient_test.go: rewrite, other origins, CheckIssuer table, go-oidc discovery and oauth2 exchange through WithHTTPClient, limits (see acceptance). Run them and see them fail (package missing).
2. `go get` go-oidc v3 and golang.org/x/oauth2 at exact versions at least two weeks old; add the `internal/identity` class, zone and the two S3 manifest entries to architecture.yaml; run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture`.
3. Create internal/identity/doc.go and internal/identity/httpclient.go: HTTPClientConfig, NewHTTPClient, the rewriting RoundTripper, CheckIssuer, WithHTTPClient.
4. Run `go test -race ./internal/identity` and `govulncheck ./...`; fix until green.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestHTTPClientRewrite` passes: with issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex` (nothing listens there) and InternalIssuerURL set to an httptest server, a GET and a POST aimed at `http://localhost:5556/dex/token` reach the httptest server, which records the path and query, a `Host: localhost:5556` header, a custom header and the POST body byte-for-byte unchanged; the caller's request object is not mutated. Red first: it fails before the RoundTripper exists.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestHTTPClientOtherOriginsUntouched` passes: a request to a second httptest origin, and to the issuer host on a different port, is not rewritten (the internal server records zero requests), and with an empty InternalIssuerURL nothing is rewritten.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestCheckIssuer` passes with a table: https accepted without an internal URL; http refused without one (error names `internalIssuerURL`); http accepted with one; an internal URL with a path such as `/dex`, a query, userinfo or an ftp scheme refused; an internal URL without an issuer refused; an issuer with a query, fragment or userinfo and a relative issuer refused. Red first: the http-without-internal row fails against a version that accepts http.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestOIDCDiscoveryKeepsIssuer` passes: an httptest server behind the internal origin serves a discovery document whose `issuer` is `http://localhost:5556/dex` (endpoints on the public origin) and a JWKS; `oidc.NewProvider(identity.WithHTTPClient(ctx, c), issuer)` succeeds (go-oidc's issuer check passes) and a token with `iss` equal to the public issuer verifies; the same call without WithHTTPClient fails (red first).
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestOAuth2ExchangeUsesClient` passes: `oauth2.Config{Endpoint: {TokenURL: "http://localhost:5556/dex/token"}}.Exchange(identity.WithHTTPClient(ctx, c), "code")` reaches the internal server's `/dex/token` with the form body unchanged, and an internal 302 is not followed.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestHTTPClientLimits` passes: with `HTTP_PROXY` set via t.Setenv the request still goes direct (Proxy=nil), a body over 1 MiB fails, a slow server hits the timeout, and no redirect is followed.
- [ ] `grep -rniE 'insecure|skipverify' internal/identity` prints nothing (no escape hatch), and `go test -race ./internal/identity` passes.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` passes with the new class, zone and both manifest entries, and `scripts/check.sh` passes, including govulncheck with the new dependencies.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-DEX-03`](dex-oidc.md#36--w-p1-dex-03) Document Dex as Warden's IdP with connector, failure-mode and prod guidance; [`W-P1-SSO-03`](console-sso-rbac.md#311--w-p1-sso-03) Implement OIDC login and callback with PKCE on the control plane; [`W-P1-VRFY-01`](identity-verification.md#112--w-p1-vrfy-01) Add internal/identity OIDC verifier with lazy JWKS, cache and config
